data.name: Kartar
data.gender_notes: Kartar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Kartar is a name derived from Sanskrit origin, meaning 'God's gift' or 'creator'. In Hindu mythology, Kartikeya or Lord Murugan, the god of war, is the most famous bearer of this name. He is the younger son of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati, and is worshipped for his wisdom, courage, and strength. The name Kartar carries the meaning “God's gift, creator” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kartar usually hope their child will grow to embody god's gift, creator and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kartar carries significant cultural importance in Hinduism as it is associated with popular deities such as Lord Kartikeya (also known as Lord Murugan and Subramanya). As a patron god of warriors, Kartikeya is revered for his military prowess, intelligence, and leadership skills, inspiring devotees to strive for excellence in their endeavors. Famous temples dedicated to Kartikeya can be found across India and parts of Southeast Asia. Cultural festivals such as the Skanda Shashti in India and the Thaipusam in Sri Lanka celebrate the God's healing power, strength, and devotion.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Kartar holds immense spiritual significance as it symbolizes the divine gift of existence bestowed upon us by deities. Given its connection to Lord Kartikeya, it also represents the divine grace and protection bestowed upon an individual. A compelling myth about Lord Kartikeya and his six faces reveals his multi-faceted strengths – wisdom, perception, spiritual development, valor, devotion, and bliss. Embracing the essence of this name, thereby, is believed to invoke the qualities of wisdom, bravery, and grace within the carrier.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kartar symbolizes the Creator or the Doer in Hinduism. The name signifies the one who creates, sustains, and transforms the universe, embodying the divine will and action. It is a reminder of the divine presence and power shaping our lives.

historical_references.reference: Kartar is an alternative name for Lord Krishna in Sikhism. The name 'Kartar' comes from the Sanskrit word 'Kartr', meaning 'doer' or 'maker'. In Hindu mythology, Lord Krishna is known as the 'Doer of the Yoga'.
historical_references.time_period: Classical Period (4th Century BC - 3rd Century AD)

historical_references.reference: The name 'Kartar' also appeared in the 16th century in Punjab when the Sikh Gurus began using it as an alternate name for Lord Krishna. The Sikhs revered Lord Krishna as an incarnation of God.
